blocks.text: 7. Match the entries of Column A with those of Column B.

Column A Column B
(i) E = \frac{hc}{\lambda} (A) Rutherford
(ii) mvr = \frac{nh}{2\pi} (B) J. J. Thomson
(iii) \alpha-ray scattering experiment (C) Max Planck
(iv) Thinly spread positively charged mass (D) Niels Bohr

8. The sum of electrons present in the second and fourth shells is equal to the
number of electrons in the third shell of an element and the fifth shell is
valence shell. Find out the number of core electrons in B.
(a) 18 (b) 19 (c) 38 (d) 36

9. A dinegative ion of an element has protons whose mass is equal to 14,696
times that of an electron. The number of neutrons is more than the number
of protons by 2. What could be the mass number?
(a) 16 (b) 8 (c) 18 (d) 10

10. The same amount of energy is required to remove an electron from the
respective orbits of hydrogen atom and $\mathrm{He}^+$ ion. Identify the orbits.

(a) $n = 2; n = 1$                                (b) $n = 2; n = 3$
(c) $n = 2; n = 4$                                (d) $n = 4; n = 1$

11. In Millikan’s oil drop experiment, the charges on the oil drops A, B and C
are 0.3 C, 0.12 C and 0.18 C, respectively. What would be the number of elec-
trons attached to these oil drops?

(a) 3, 12, 18 (b) 6, 24, 38
(c) 5, 2, 3 (d) 6, 4, 9

12. An element exists in the form of two isotopes with mass numbers $x$ and $x +$
2. If the percentage abundance of these isotopes is 75.77% and 24.23%, then
what is the average atomic mass of the element?

(a) $x + 0.5$ (b) $x + 0.25$
(c) $x + 0.75$ (d) $x + 1$

13. Deuterium is an isotope of hydrogen. Calculate the specific charge of deu-
teron (charge of electron = $1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C; mass of proton = $1.67 \times 10^{-27}$ kg;
mass of neutron = $1.72 \times 10^{-27}$ kg)

(a) $2.3 \times 10^7$ C/kg (b) $1.15 \times 10^7$ C/kg
(c) $0.575 \times 10^8$ C/kg (d) $3.45 \times 10^8$ C/kg
